Attendance by day, and the muster roll for the whole month, fill themselves from those messages. No register to copy out.
B O Q and budget. Your B O Q with client and budget rates per line. What is different: progress comes from the site's WhatsApp updates, not a measurement sheet.
B O Q and budget. Your estimate, line by line, with what the client pays and what it should cost you. Bring it in from the Excel you already have.
BOQ line. One item of work in the BOQ: what it is, its unit, how much, and the rate the client pays.. 4.1 Plastering, 1,200 sqm at ₹420 a sqm.
BOQ section. A group of BOQ lines for one part of the building, like Earthwork or Plastering.
BOQ. Every work item of the project with its quantity and rate: the project's price and its budget.. PCC 1:4:8, 42 cum at ₹5,800.

Before a building starts, it is priced piece by piece. So much concrete, so much plastering, each at a price. That list is called the B O Q, the bill of quantities. This page is that list, and how far the site has got on each piece.
Bills and checks. Their bill against the work measured and the rate agreed, less advances and retention. Approve it, or send it back with why.
Bring your Excel. One row per item, with Description, Unit, Qty and Rate. I read the rows and show you what I understood before anything is saved.
Budget cost. What the work should cost you to build: your own cost rate for each line, added up. Less than the contract value is your profit.
Check what came in. Lines priced shows how many lines still have no client rate or no budget rate after the upload. Fill those in to see the margin.
Contract value. What the client pays you for all the work in the BOQ: each line's quantity times its rate, added up.
Cost centre. The bucket a cost is counted in (materials, labour, fuel, equipment).
Cube test. A test that crushes sample concrete cubes at 7 and 28 days to check strength.
Cum. Volumes: 1 cum (cubic metre) is about 35.3 cft (cubic feet); 1 brass is 100 cft.
Curing. Keeping new concrete or plaster wet for days so it gains strength.
DPR. A site's day on one page: who came, what work was done, what material came or ran out, what is stuck.. Mesiri makes it every evening from the WhatsApp updates.
Defects period. The time after handover when the contractor must fix defects.
Delivered, no bill. Material that came with no bill yet. When the bill comes, match it to those deliveries, so nothing is paid twice or for what never came.
Delivery challan. The supplier's delivery note that comes with the lorry.
Each B O Q section becomes a bar on the schedule. Quick plan lines them up one after another in a minute.
Earned so far. The value of the work already done: what the client owes you for it at the BOQ rates.
Estimate. The expected quantities and cost of the work, before or alongside the BOQ.
Every bill and payment. A bill from a shop, diesel, a hired machine, tea for the site: each is an expense here, with its photo, its project and its category.
Every day, the site tells Mesiri who came. That one message is all it takes: attendance, the muster roll and the wages all follow from it.
Every evening, each site's daily progress report is made for you, and sent to you and to your client. Nobody has to sit and type it up.

Every line is one piece of work, with its quantity and its rates. Here's the useful part: when the site reports work on WhatsApp, it counts against the right line by itself, and you see how much of the budget that work has earned.
For labour, material and subcontractors: the budget, what the work has earned, and what you've actually spent. Side by side.
For the plan to work, it needs to know what each B O Q line uses, like bags of cement per cubic metre of concrete. Fill the common ones in one tap, or set them on the B O Q.
Free-issue material. Material the client supplies to the contractor, which must be accounted for.
GRN. The record of material accepted at site: what came, how much, from whom.
GST. Goods and services tax, added to most bills; a GST-registered business can claim it back.
GSTIN. A business's GST registration number, printed on its bills and letterhead.

Pick a project. This page works on one project at a time. Pick it here, or in the bar at the top.
QS. The person who measures work and prepares and checks bills and costs.
Quantity times the client's price. The gold bar shows how big this line is next to the others in its section, so the big money stands out.
Quick check. One line costs more to build than the client pays for it. Its margin is in red. Tap that line.
Quick check. One line loses money on every unit it builds. Can you find it? Tap it.
RA bill. A stage bill to the client for the work measured so far.. RA-03: ground-floor slab and brickwork, ₹8.4 L.
RCC. Reinforced cement concrete: concrete with steel bars inside, for columns, beams and slabs.
Rate. The price for one unit of work: per sqm of plaster, per cum of concrete.
Reconciliation. What should have been used for the work done, compared with what was actually used.
Retention. A share of each bill the client holds back until the defects period ends.
Schedule from the B O Q. Sections become schedule activities: no separate WBS to keep in step.
Send this to Mesiri, just like Ravi would. A card comes back. Tap Save, and I'll watch for it here.
Shuttering. The temporary mould of plywood or steel that holds wet concrete until it sets.
Site engineer. The person on site every day who runs the work and reports it.
Site work to map. Like mapping D P R quantities to B O Q items, except I propose the line. Add all accepts them.
Slab. A flat concrete floor or roof.
Stock register. The running record of what came in, what went out, and what is left, per item.
Stock shows what each site holds right now. Movements is the full story: every delivery, every use, every transfer that changed it.
Subcontractor. A team or firm you give part of the work to, paid by work done.. A tiling team paid per sq ft.
TDS. Income tax the client keeps back from each bill and pays to the government for you; you claim it when you file tax.. 2% TDS on a ₹10 lakh bill: ₹20,000 kept back.

Welcome to Green Villa Builders. This is your own sample company, with two projects and two weeks of site work already recorded. Nothing here is real, and nobody gets a message. So go ahead and try anything.
What you keep. Client rate minus budget cost. Green: healthy. Orange: thin, under 5%. Red: this line loses money.
What you keep. The client's price minus your cost: the money this line leaves you. Green is healthy. Orange means very little is left. Red means this line loses money.
What you owe each supplier. Their bills less what you paid, what is overdue, and what you paid ahead.
When someone takes money in advance, it's kept against their name, and it comes off their next wages by itself. No more notebooks.
When the lorry arrives, the delivery is received against its order. That's the goods received note. Now the order, the stock and the supplier's bill all agree, so nobody pays for what never came.
